newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dubinin sees T-bill yield at 20 pct by end year.
newsitem.headline: Dubinin sees T-bill yield at 20 pct by end year.

text.p: Yields on Russian Treasury bills should fall to 20 percent by the end of the year if 1997 inflation is on target at 12 percent, Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Tuesday.

The average yield on an issue of 364-day GKO discount Treasury bills last Wednesday was 26.98 percent. The average yield of T-bills in secondary trade was 25.1 percent on Monday, the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX) said.
"The favourable trend by which the prices of borrowing on the domestic and foreign markets are drawing together is continuing," Dubinin told a meeting of senior Finance Ministry officials.
"The interest rate on T-bills and bonds is now less than 28 percent, and we can forecast that it will be 20 percent by the end of the year," he said.

This would be possible if the inflation rate targeted in the 1997 budget is reached, he said. The budget assumes year-on-year inflation of 12 percent in December this year, down from 21.8 percent in 1996.
